messages:
nora: Trying to onboard a customer with an M1 fleet image and hit a bunch of packaging pains. `pip install redwood-sdk` on mac arm falls back to sdist, building takes >15m in our builder because the sdist triggers PEP 517 build isolation. wheel available in PyPI only for manylinux_x86_64.

nora: Error excerpt:
```
ERROR: redwood_sdk-1.0.0-cp311-cp311-manylinux2014_x86_64.whl is not a supported wheel on this platform.
Building wheels for collected packages: redwood-sdk
  Building wheel for redwood-sdk (pyproject.toml) ... done
  Created wheel for redwood-sdk: filename=redwood_sdk-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl size=123456 sha256=...
  Stored in directory: /tmp/pip-req-build-xxxx
Successfully built redwood-sdk
Installing collected packages: redwood-sdk
  Running setup.py install for redwood-sdk ... done
```

sam: Ugh. That explains the huge image build times. Do you also see missing type markers? We require `py.typed` for strict typing in our base images.

nora: Yep — mypy flags `Module 'redwood_sdk' has no attribute 'client'` and IDE doesn't recognize inline types. I inspected the wheel and there is no `py.typed` in the package root.

tess: Quick checklist: (1) Which build backend are you using (setuptools/poetry/flit)? (2) Are universal2 mac wheels being published from CI? We recently changed the mac matrix and might have dropped universal builds.

nora: pyproject shows `build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"` and MANIFEST.in might be incomplete. Our GH Actions currently only runs manylinux build on linux runners; macos runners were accidental opt-out.

ci-bot: CI note: macos-latest matrix was disabled in release pipeline on 1.0.0 due to a label mismatch.

sam: For immediate installs you can `pip install --no-build-isolation --no-use-pep517 redwood-sdk==1.0.0` if the environment has build deps preinstalled, or `pip install git+https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk@main` to pull the latest artifact (we have arm wheels on main from GH Actions). Not great for customers though.

nora: We also saw a poetry/constraints clash when building a wheel in our monorepo: `poetry lock` produced a different resolution than `pip-compile` used by our image tooling. That made two versions of `httpx` appear depending on the pipeline which is terrifying.

tess: We should: (a) ensure MANIFEST.in includes `redwood_sdk/py.typed`, (b) add universal2 macOS wheel to release CI (macos-12/macOS-13), (c) add a validation job that installs the released wheel on arm64 runners and on a minimal builder to catch sdist-only regressions, (d) add a `packaging.md` note about constraints/poetry gotchas.

gwen: I'll open a release hotfix PR: include py.typed, pin build-system requires to setuptools >=65, add `sdist` and `bdist_wheel` matrix artifacts, and patch the GH workflow to include macos matrix. Also add a smoke test that runs `pip install redwood-sdk==${{ release_version }}` inside macOS arm64 runner.

nora: Thanks. If you can also add a note about editable installs — `pip install -e .` under Poetry can yield different transitive deps because of `extras` mapping. We had an incident where `pip install -e .` in CI pulled `optional-dep>=2.0` while `poetry install` pulled `optional-dep==1.9` from the lockfile. That broke runtime tests.

sam: For the lockfile issue, our image build should prefer installing from a constraints file generated by `poetry export -f requirements.txt --without-hashes` and then `pip install -r constraints.txt --no-deps` before installing package. I'll draft a short HOWTO.

ci-bot: Created GH issue #2378: "Packaging: publish mac universal2 and include py.typed; add wheel validation on arm runners" -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/issues/2378

gwen: Assigning to @tess for CI changes and @lisa for MANIFEST fix. Nora, can you validate on your M1 once the fix is published?

nora: Yup, I'll test both `pip install redwood-sdk==1.0.1` and `pip install git+https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk@main` and report back. Cheers! :white_check_mark:
